needs: LEAP environment (official repository at commit 3f7e440 as used for the reported runs, run_docker.sh)
pseudo labels on the training split from the standardized detector (README step 4)
cross-frame association (re-identification) model: dataset generation (vehicle_reid/generate_reid.py) and training (vehicle_reid/run.sh)
motion-pattern library from training trajectories (traj_cluster/, track_cluster.py)
per-dataset configuration file (configs/<dataset>.yaml); no distilled detector, per section 7
confirm with the LEAP operator which steps the reported runs executed and on which splits
OTIF environment (_archive/otif Docker image, conda env otif, Go toolchain) with the standardized detector (YOLOv5 on CalDoT1/2 and Amsterdam, B3D RetinaNet), as in the reported runs
reference detection on the training split (pipeline2/10_detect.go) and IoU tracks for the recurrent-tracker split, which section 7 sets to the training split (iou-tracker2.go)
proxy training: frame extraction (pipeline/16_extract_frames.py) and segmentation-proxy training at each proxy resolution (pipeline/20_train_segmentation.py)
parameter tuning on the validation split (pipeline2/30_speed_accuracy.go)
B3D datasets: OTIF-format copies of jnc0/2/6/7 are not under /otif-dataset; locate the converted data used for the reported runs

import json, sys, time
import torch
import polyis.models.detector
dataset, out, loads = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
start = time.time()
torch.zeros(1, device='cuda')
torch.cuda.synchronize()
cuda_init_s = time.time() - start
times = []
for _ in range(loads):
    begin = time.time()
    detector = polyis.models.detector.get_detector(dataset, 0, batch_size=16, num_images=0)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times.append(time.time() - begin)
    del detector
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
with open(out, 'a') as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(dict(dataset=dataset, start=start, end=time.time(), device=torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
                            cuda_init_s=cuda_init_s, load_s=times)) + '\n')

import torch
import polyis.models.detector
dataset, out, loads = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
start = time.time()
torch.zeros(1, device='cuda')
torch.cuda.synchronize()
cuda_init_s = time.time() - start
times = []
for _ in range(loads):
    begin = time.time()
    detector = polyis.models.detector.get_detector(dataset, 0, batch_size=16, num_images=0)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times.append(time.time() - begin)
    del detector
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
with open(out, 'a') as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(dict(dataset=dataset, start=start, end=time.time(), device=torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
                            cuda_init_s=cuda_init_s, load_s=times)) + '\n')

classifier_optimization.basis: estimate: gap since the previous resolution group finished in the same p015 run
classifier_optimization.unit: process seconds of one benchmark process

classifier_training.basis: recorded: fine-tuning epochs; instrumented and process: wall clock of both stages from file timestamps
classifier_training.unit: process seconds of one training process

mistrack_profiling.basis: estimate: elapsed time from output modification times x min(40 workers, videos), an upper bound on process seconds
mistrack_profiling.unit: process seconds, upper bound (elapsed x min(40 workers, videos))

reference_detection_train.basis: recorded: p011 times each frame's read and detect; process: recorded (file creation times are stale on some datasets); detector loading per video is not recorded
reference_detection_train.note: p011 detects in batches of 16; the reference pipeline detects one frame at a time
reference_detection_train.unit: process seconds, summed over work units (single-worker equivalent, not elapsed time)

reference_outputs_valid.basis: recorded: read, detect, and track per frame; process: estimate, detection from its runtime file's creation to detection.jsonl's last write (not below the recorded ops), tracking as recorded
reference_outputs_valid.unit: process seconds, summed over work units (single-worker equivalent, not elapsed time)

training_data_creation.basis: recorded: split and save per frame; process: estimate from each video's runtime file creation to last write (adds the untimed seek, decode, and detection parsing)
training_data_creation.unit: process seconds, summed over work units (single-worker equivalent, not elapsed time)

validation_scoring.basis: estimate: test-split p110 seconds per (configuration, video) x validation configurations x videos
validation_scoring.unit: process seconds (one TrackEval process per configuration)

validation_sweep.basis: recorded; process: estimate from file timestamps
validation_sweep.unit: process seconds, summed over work units (single-worker equivalent, not elapsed time)

not_recorded.detector_loading: detector loading and warm-up per p011 video, per reference video, and per p040 configuration are not recorded; outside both boundaries on both sides
not_recorded.first_unit_of_each_task: process time of the first video of each sweep task is max(own span, recorded): it misses work done before its output directory was created
not_recorded.tradeoff_and_pareto: p130 tradeoff and p135 Pareto selection write no timings (they read one score table)
not_recorded.training_data_pruning: p013 (deletes never-relevant tiles' training images) writes no timings

mistrack_profiling.basis: measured: p016 re-run with one worker, its wall clock (the process seconds of its profiles)

cache.basis: estimate: elapsed time from output modification times x min(40 workers, videos), an upper bound on process seconds

reference_detection_train.basis: measured: p011 re-run, each video's detections file from creation (after the detector loads) to last write, summed

cache.basis: recorded: p011 times each frame's read and detect; process: recorded (file creation times are stale on some datasets); detector loading per video is not recorded

reference_detection_train.unit: process seconds, summed over work units (single-worker equivalent, not elapsed time)

training_data_creation.basis: cross-check, not substituted: p012 re-run, each video's runtime file from creation to last write, summed; its workers (up to 20, one per training video) share the run's CPU set (run.own_cpus of run.cpu_set_size busy), so the spans include contention among them

cache.basis: recorded: split and save per frame; process: estimate from each video's runtime file creation to last write (adds the untimed seek, decode, and detection parsing)

training_data_creation.unit: process seconds, summed over work units (single-worker equivalent, not elapsed time)

training_data_pruning.basis: measured: p013 re-run's wall clock (one process); its work depends on which per-video relevance bitmaps p012's race on always_relevant/ leaves (finding 10), so it removed a different number of training images than the cache's run (files_removed_over_cache), on whose output the classifier was trained

validation_scoring.basis: measured: p110 --valid re-run, each configuration task's span (output directory creation to last result file), summed, at 16 TrackEval processes on 40 CPUs (deployed: 0.8 per CPU, 64 on ace's 80; the estimate's test-split runs were at that density)

cache.basis: estimate: test-split p110 seconds per (configuration, video) x validation configurations x videos

validation_scoring.unit: process seconds (one TrackEval process per configuration)

detector_loading.basis: measured: get_detector as p040 calls it, in a fresh process (CUDA start-up, then constructions), without p040's warm-up; it passes batch_size 16 and num_images 0 where p040 passes 4 and the first video's image count, which only polyis's yolov3 detector reads (these datasets use ultralytics and RetinaNet)
detector_loading.note: not added to any total: detector loading is outside both boundaries on both sides (p011 and the reference pipeline load once per video process, p040 once per configuration); p011_cold_loads_s is what one cold load per training video would add to preparation

import json, sys, time
import torch
import polyis.models.detector
dataset, out, loads = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
start = time.time()
torch.zeros(1, device='cuda')
torch.cuda.synchronize()
cuda_init_s = time.time() - start
times = []
for _ in range(loads):
    begin = time.time()
    detector = polyis.models.detector.get_detector(dataset, 0, batch_size=16, num_images=0)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    times.append(time.time() - begin)
    del detector
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
with open(out, 'a') as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(dict(dataset=dataset, start=start, end=time.time(), device=torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),

boundaries.instrumented: p121's counted ops minus per-frame video decoding (VIDEO_DECODE_OPS), on preparation and on both pipelines' extraction; components without op records at their process time
boundaries.process: whole-process time per work unit from file timestamps (sweep, p012, reference detection on both pipelines' sides); recorded time for p011 (stale creation times) and the reference's tracking; components without op records at their process time; detector loading is outside on both sides
boundaries.recorded: recorded op times only: p121's boundary as is, classifier fine-tuning epochs only, sweep unscaled, no estimates; a lower bound

host.note: the host this script ran on, which holds the cache and ran its stages; the re-timed components ran on bombe (retiming.components.*.run.host, physical_gpu, and cpus); GPUs are those present when this script ran

retiming.p110_density: p110_density: optional p110 re-run at the deployed 0.8 TrackEval processes per CPU, reported in validation_scoring.density_cross_check and never substituted
retiming.runs: per dataset and step, the latest record that exited 0 among those without foreign GPU samples, else the latest that exited 0 (flagged in gpu_contaminated_steps); attempts counts all records; each chosen record's launcher run must have a summary in launcher_runs.jsonl

method.unit: process seconds, summed over work units (single-worker equivalent, not elapsed time)
